title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
abstract: arXiv:2610.31791v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. Unlike plain text, page images retain figures, layout, and presentation. This signal is robust, surviving smaller models and even compressing the whole paper into a single image. translated_abstract: 自动化研究在很大程度上通过基准测试性能来评估，但研究的价值很少能简化为一个单一的分数。人类通过同行评审来判断一项工作的整体贡献，而这难以建模，因为它充满噪声且依赖于众多因素。然而，如果仅凭论文本身，我们就能直接预测其同行评审结果呢？我们提出了PaperScorer，这是一系列模型，可以从论文提取的文本或页面截图中预测论文的录用或拒稿决定，训练时仅使用决策结果，并去除了作者身份和格式上的捷径。视觉模型最具预测性（在ICLR论文上达到68%的准确率，在arXiv的ML论文上达到77%），超越了纯文本模型和前沿推理模型。与纯文本不同，页面图像保留了图表、布局和呈现方式。这一信号是稳健的，在更小的模型上依然有效，甚至可以将整篇论文压缩为单张图像。但准确的预测并非均匀分布……
tldr: 该论文提出PaperScorer系列模型，仅凭论文文本或页面截图即可预测同行评审的录用或拒稿结果，其中视觉模型表现最佳（ICLR论文68%、arXiv机器学习论文77%准确率），表明论文的图表、布局与呈现方式蕴含着重要的评审决策信号。
en_tdlr: PaperScorer models predict peer-review accept/reject decisions directly from paper text or page screenshots, with vision models performing best (68% accuracy on ICLR and 77% on arXiv ML papers), showing that figures, layout, and presentation carry strong signals about review outcomes.
